heroHeadline: GALATI: RUSSIA STRIKES NATO APARTMENT BUILDING WITH GERAN-2 DRONE — CIVILIAN CASUALTIES ON ALLIANCE TERRITORY; RUTTE 'EVERY INCH' PLEDGE; ROMANIA EXPELS RUSSIAN CONSUL FROM CONSTANTA
heroSubtitle: On the night of May 28–29, 2026, a Russian Geran-2 drone (Shahed-136 variant) crossed Romanian airspace and struck a 10-story residential apartment building in Galati — a Danube city 200 km from the Ukrainian border — injuring two civilians and prompting evacuation of 70 residents. It was the 28th breach of Romanian airspace and the first to cause civilian casualties on NATO territory since Russia's full-scale invasion began. Romanian F-16s scrambled but did not intercept. NATO Secretary General Rutte immediately called Romanian President Nicusor Dan and affirmed: 'NATO is ready to defend every inch of allied territory... Russia's reckless behavior poses a danger to us all.' US Ambassador to NATO Matthew Whitaker echoed: 'We will defend every inch of NATO territory.' No formal Article 5 consultation was invoked. Romania responded with its sharpest direct diplomatic action against Russia since 2022: expelling the Russian Consul-General from Constanta, closing the Russian Consulate General there, summoning the Russian ambassador, and formally requesting NATO expedite anti-drone capability transfers to Romanian forces. The incident arrives 39 days before the Ankara Leaders' Summit (July 7–8) and directly alongside the unresolved crisis at its core: the same US military whose ambassador pledged 'every inch' defense has confirmed it will contribute zero drones to NATO's eastern flank (Der Spiegel, May 26), while jets, bombers, and submarines are simultaneously cut. Romania hosts a France-led NATO Enhanced Forward Presence battlegroup but lacks the counter-drone density to consistently intercept low-flying Shahed drones over its Danube delta territory. The Galati strike injects a concrete kinetic dimension into the NATO-US tensions crisis just as Rutte's pre-Ankara diplomatic circuit continues — he met Bulgarian PM Radev the day before the strike, and the Ankara summit agenda now includes NATO's first civilian casualties from a Russian drone attack on alliance soil.
